title: Coffee brewer for both hot coffee and cold coffee drinks and smoothies with one major design flaw
text:
Coffee brewer for both hot coffee and cold coffee drinks and smoothies with one major design flaw. I am pleasantly surprised by this machine except for one major design flaw I outline in the CONS section below. It brews a great cup of coffee and also has a not-so-strong blender that brews coffee drinks and fruit smoothies.

I made a cup of coffee for my boyfriend and a classic coffee frappe, using the recipe in the booklet, for both me and him. My boyfriend and I loved the results. I especially loved the frappe. Below are the pros and cons that I found with this machine.

PROS
- Setup is easy

- Brewing a cup of coffee is simple--just add a tablespoon of coffee for each cup of water to the brew basket (a paper filter is needed), and fill the "thermos mug" with water, pour that in the unit, put the mug under the brew basket, and power on the unit. Note that the mug holds about 1-1/2 cups so that would be about a tablespoon and a half depending on taste preferences.

- Brewing a cold drink is also simple. The steps above are repeated but about 6 tablespoons of coffee (depending on the recipe) and less water is used. For the classic coffee frappe only 1 cup of water is used during the brew cycle. Add the brewed coffee and other ingredients to the blender, pulse a few times, then blend on high until done and a wonderful frappe is created.

- The instructions are well written and 10 recipes are included which includes 4 non-coffee recipes such as strawberry banana and pineapple peach smoothies.

- All parts are easily washed; even though the blender blade does not come out.

- The blender holds 32 ounces of liquid and the measurements are marked on the plastic.

- The "thermos mug" is very nice, has a good grip, and the lip on the cover makes it easy to drink from.

- After the brew cycle is done, only a few beads of water are left behind in the reservoir. Many other coffee makers I've tried leave behind a tablespoon or more.

- The spigot the water flows through sits behind a tab that holds it in place. This is excellent because it raises and lowers automatically each time the lid is open and shut.

CONS

- The classic coffee frappe called for 6 tablespoons of coffee to only one cup of water. As a result, when the brew cycle was done, not all the grinds were wet. Therefore, in my opinion the amount of water was not enough to saturate and brew such a large amount of coffee. I think if the spigot on the brewer was a bit larger or more water was used, this would be resolved. This is the biggest design flaw in my opinion and the main reason I brought this down to 3 stars. I've also reduced the coffee grinds and that still didn't help.

- The unit does feel like it's made of cheap plastic; but then again it is rare that products on the market today do not feel this way.

- Only crescent-shaped ice cubes (typically ones made by a refrigerator ice receptacle) should be used in the blender. I used the square ice cubes from an ice cube tray and the ice did not break down as easily.

- I was unable to use both the hot and cold cycle at the same time. What I mean by this is that while the unit was brewing, I decided to turn on the blender to see what would happen. Immediately the brewing cycle turned off. I had to stop the blender and turn the brewing cycle back on to finish the coffee brew cycle. I did not see any warning in the manual not to operate both sides. However, based on my tests, only one side can be used at the same time.

- No coffee filters were provided with the unit. The unit takes a cupcake style filter that looks like it's a size 4. I suppose a size 2 can be used as well. I only had a size 4 cone filter on hand so I flattened it and used that as a temporary solution. It would have been nice if Hamilton Beach had included at least a 5-filter sample pack with each unit.

Amazon's currently listed price is $69.99 for this machine. Personally, that is a bit steep. I think a good price for this unit is between $30 and $40; however, price is subjective based on how much such a unit is worth to the buyer.

In summary, I would have been very impressed with this java blend coffee brewer had it not had that design flaw. I do, however, love its versatility and the fact that a cup of coffee can be directly brewed into a "thermos mug" for immediate travel and it blends delicious cold drinks as well.
